verification: limactl shell local-dev -- sh -c 'cd ~/openlore && cargo test -p xtask --test scale_to_zero_ci'

facts.F1: Strip x-amzn-errortype in the prod-indexer CloudFront response headers policy (deploy/tofu/environments/prod-indexer/edge.tf) and sample POST search response headers for x-amzn-* headers in edge_checks (deploy/indexer/lambda.sh) in addition to GET /healthz (scale-to-zero-hosting M7).
facts.F10: Inspecting the policy configuration alone does not observe a live CloudFront edge stripping x-amzn-errortype from an actual origin error response or verify that the policy is attached to the active distribution behavior.
facts.F11: The CloudFront response headers policy "strip" retains all six previously configured x-amzn-* headers in its removed headers list without dropping any of them when x-amzn-errortype is added.
facts.F12: The promise does not enumerate the six existing x-amzn-* header names, so a check verifying only header count or only x-amzn-errortype could miss a renamed, misspelled, or dropped existing header.
facts.F13: edge_checks rejects a response when a POST search response contains any x-amzn-* header (including x-amzn-errortype).
facts.F14: Checking edge_checks only against a happy-path or mocked POST search response may not observe origin error responses that emit x-amzn-errortype, mixed-case header names, or real deployed edge responses.
facts.F15: edge_checks continues to reject a response when a GET /healthz response contains any x-amzn-* header.
facts.F16: An oracle focused on the new POST search check could miss a regression in GET /healthz rejection, and edge_checks does not observe x-amzn-* header leakage on routes other than GET /healthz and POST search.
facts.F17: Inspect the prod-indexer CloudFront response headers strip policy configuration for removed origin headers
facts.F18: The strip policy removes x-amzn-errortype alongside the existing six x-amzn-* headers and no others
facts.F19: CloudFront strips x-amzn-errortype and all six existing origin headers from responses before clients see them
facts.F2: Prevent x-amzn-errortype and other origin x-amzn-* headers from leaking through the CloudFront edge on search or error responses
facts.F20: Static HCL declares all seven headers in the strip policy, while live CloudFront edge enforcement is not exercised against AWS
facts.F21: Run the edge verification check against a stubbed edge whose responses vary which endpoint carries an origin header
facts.F22: The check passes when both health check and POST search are clean, fails when POST search returns x-amzn-errortype or any mixed-case x-amzn-* header even with a clean health check, and still fails when the health check returns an x-amzn-* header
facts.F23: Deployment edge verification blocks release whenever an origin x-amzn-* header leaks on either POST search or the health check
facts.F24: POST search returns an x-amzn-* header only on a non-200 error response while 200 POST search responses remain clean
facts.F3: aws_cloudfront_response_headers_policy.strip removes x-amzn-errortype in addition to the existing six x-amzn-* headers
facts.F4: edge_checks rejects an x-amzn-* response header on POST search as well as on GET /healthz
facts.F5: openlore-index-strip removes x-amzn-errortype alongside the existing six x-amzn-* headers, and edge_checks rejects an x-amzn-* header on the POST search response as well as GET /healthz
facts.F6: Run xtask scale_to_zero_ci tests against deploy/tofu/environments/prod-indexer/edge.tf and deploy/indexer/lambda.sh edge_checks
facts.F7: openlore-index-strip includes x-amzn-errortype in remove_headers_config, and edge_checks fails when a POST search response carries x-amzn-errortype even if GET /healthz carries no x-amzn-* headers
facts.F8: openlore-index-strip omits x-amzn-errortype, or edge_checks passes when POST search returns an x-amzn-* header
facts.F9: The CloudFront response headers policy "strip" includes x-amzn-errortype in its removed headers list so that x-amzn-errortype is stripped from responses.
